title: Tool Span to LLM Tool Call Linkage
dataSources: Spans read back with `AgentStream.get(...).get_spans(limit=...)`: tool span `tool_call_id` and LLM span `output_tool_calls`
description: Checks that every tool span in Splunk Agent Observability ties back to the LLM turn that chose it: the tool span's `tool_call_id` must equal an `id` in the parent LLM span's `output_tool_calls`.
value: Investigators can only explain a bad tool run if they can see which model turn asked for it and with what arguments. Broken linkage makes Tool Selection Quality results (UC-13.8.13) hard to act on.
implementation: Put the model's chosen tool calls in the LLM span output as an assistant message with `tool_calls` and pass `finish_reason`. Log each tool span at the tool loop's call site with `tool_call_id=call.id`. Periodically read spans back and flag tool spans whose `tool_call_id` matches no LLM tool call.
visualization: Span tree in the trace view; read-back script output listing unlinked tool spans.
knownFalsePositives: Tool calls the application makes on its own (not chosen by the model) have no LLM tool call to match. Give them a distinct span name and exclude them from the check.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

A Splunk Agent Observability project for the application and one Agent Stream per environment or agent inside it. Do not create a second project for the same application: a second project splits the traces. The agent reads `SPLUNK_AO_PROJECT` and `SPLUNK_AO_AGENT_STREAM` from the environment. SaaS tenants authenticate with `SPLUNK_AO_REALM` and `SPLUNK_AO_O11Y_TOKEN`; on-prem tenants with `SPLUNK_AO_API_KEY` plus `SPLUNK_AO_CONSOLE_URL`. Install the SDK with `pip install splunk-ao` (`pip install "splunk-ao[langchain]"` for the LangChain callback).

Step 1 — Instrument the agent

In an OpenAI tool loop, put the chosen calls in the LLM span output as `{"role": "assistant", "content": ..., "tool_calls": [{"id", "function": {"name", "arguments"}}]}` and pass `finish_reason`; `tool_calls` there marks the turn that chose a tool. History items that are `ChatCompletionMessage` objects go in as `m.model_dump(exclude_none=True)`. Log tool spans in the loop, not inside the tool dispatcher: the loop has `call.id`, and importing the logger into the tools module tends to create a circular import.

Step 2 — Configure in Splunk Agent Observability

Open a trace with a tool call. The tool span should sit under the agent span, after the LLM span whose output lists the call.

Step 3 — Validate

Run the read-back check on a test stream after a request that calls a tool. In query results the tool span's `tool_call_id` equals the `id` in the parent LLM span's `output_tool_calls`. The read-back field shapes come from field testing on `splunk-ao` 0.6.1; recheck them on newer SDK versions. This use case was written from the Splunk Agent Observability documentation without access to a tenant, so it ships as a draft. Confirm each step in the Splunk Agent Observability console before promoting it.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Schedule the check daily from the team's job runner and track the unlinked count per release.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

Every tool span unlinked: the LLM span output does not include `tool_calls`, or `tool_call_id` was not passed to `add_tool_span`. Empty read-back: allow 30 to 60 seconds of indexing lag.
grandmaExplanation: For each tool the assistant used, we check we can point to the moment it decided to use it, so we can explain its choices later.

productArtifacts.title: Read-back check for unlinked tool spans
productArtifacts.body:
import json
from splunk_ao import AgentStream

s = AgentStream.get(name=stream_name, project_name=project_name)
spans = s.get_spans(limit=200)

chosen = set()
for sp in spans:
    calls = sp.get("output_tool_calls")
    if calls:
        for c in (json.loads(calls) if isinstance(calls, str) else calls):
            chosen.add(c["id"])

unlinked = [sp for sp in spans if sp.get("tool_call_id") and sp["tool_call_id"] not in chosen]
print(f"{len(unlinked)} tool spans with no matching LLM tool call")
